description:
ERECTION OF A  FIRST FLOOR REAR EXTENSION
AND REAR MANSARD ROOF EXTENSION WITH DORMER WINDOWS, ALTERATINS TO SINGLE STOREY REAR EXTENSION TO FLAT ROOF, INSERTION OF FRONT
ROOFLIGHTS AND CONVERSION OF THE FIRST AND SECOND FLOOR FROM SELF CONTAINED
FLAT ( CLASS C3) TO X3 BEDSITS (CLASS C4), ALTERATIONS TO CHIMNEY, SHOP FRONT INCLUDING INSERTION OF FRONT
DOOR, PROVISION OF AMENITY SPACE, CYCLE STORAGE AND BIN AREA TO
REAR (PART RETROSPECTIVE)
subdivision_of_building: Part ground floor, First floor and Loft floor
decision_conditions:
<p class="MsoListParagraph" style="">By reason of absence of As Designed internal
water calculations and specifications for any proposed water fittings to
demonstrate the development will achieve internal water usage of less than 105
litres per person per day, the applicant has failed to demonstrate that the
application would meet the requirement of National Decision-Making 2026 Policy
CC1and Merton Local Plan 2024 policy CC2.6.<o:p></o:p></p>

<p class="MsoListParagraph">The proposed Flats 1 and 2, by reason of their
inadequate internal floorspace, would fail to provide an acceptable standard of
residential accommodation, resulting in a cramped and unsatisfactory living
environment to the detriment of the amenities of future occupiers. The proposal
is therefore contrary to National Decision-Making 2026 Policy P3, London Plan 2021
Policy D6 , Merton Local Plan 2024 Policies D12.1 and D12.3, and the Nationally
Described Space Standard (2015).<o:p></o:p></p>

<p class="MsoListParagraph">In the absence of a completed Section 106 legal
agreement securing affordable housing contributions, and in the absence of a
Financial Viability Assessment demonstrating that such provision would render
the development unviable, the proposal fails to make appropriate provision
towards affordable housing. The proposal is therefore contrary to London Plan 2021Policies
H4 and H5 and Strategic Policy H11.1 of the Merton Local Plan 2024.<o:p></o:p></p>

<p class="MsoNormal">In the absence of a completed S106 undertaking to ensure
that additional flats over and above the number of units currently on the site
are prevented from being able to obtain parking permits for the Controlled
Parking Zone, the proposal would result in an increased demand for on street
parking, resulting in a detrimental impact on highway and additional parking
pressure locally and be contrary to the Mayor and the Council's commitment to
reducing car usage and promoting more sustainable forms of transport. The
proposal would therefore be contrary to National Decision-Making 2026 Policy T1,
London Plan 2021 Policies T6 and T6.1, and Merton Local Plan 2024 Policies
T16.3 and T16.4.<o:p></o:p></p>

<p class="MsoListParagraph" style="">By reason of absence of a completed Good Homes
Alliance Overheating Risk Tool, Dynamic overheating modelling outputs or other
supporting information demonstrating how the risk of overheating has been
mitigated the proposal fails to comply with National Decision-Making 2026 Policy
P3 and Merton Local Plan 2024 policies CC2.1, D12.2 and D12.3.<o:p></o:p></p>

<p class="MsoListParagraph" style="margin-bottom: 0cm; line-height: 15pt;"><span style="font-variant-numeric: normal; font-variant-east-asian: normal; font-variant-alternates: normal; font-variant-position: normal; font-variant-emoji: normal; font-size-adjust: none; font-language-override: normal; font-kerning: auto; font-optical-sizing: auto; font-feature-settings: normal; font-variation-settings: normal; font-stretch: normal; line-height: normal;">&nbsp;</span><!--[endif]-->In the absence of robust and
satisfactory evidence to demonstrate that the significant loss of Class E
commercial floorspace would not adversely impact upon the vitality and
viability of the commercial unit and the Colliers Wood High Street
Neighbourhood Parade, and that the extent of floorspace loss proposed
represents the minimum necessary to facilitate the residential accommodation,
the proposal is contrary to National Decision-Making Policy 2026 L1, and
Policies DM E1, DM R1 and DM R4 of the Merton Local Plan 2024.<font face="Segoe UI, sans-serif"><span style="font-size: 10.5pt;"><o:p></o:p></span></font></p>

<p class="MsoListParagraph" style="margin-bottom: 0cm; line-height: 15pt;">By reason of the unsatisfactory
design, layout and accessibility of the proposed cycle storage, the development
would fail to provide convenient, fit for purpose cycle parking and would not
effectively encourage cycling as a sustainable mode of transport. The proposal
is therefore contrary to National Decision-Making 2026 Policy T1, London Plan 2021
Policy T5 and Merton Local Plan 2024 Policies D12.3, T16.1 and T16.2.<font face="Segoe UI, sans-serif"><span style="font-size: 10.5pt;"><o:p></o:p></span></font></p>

<p class="MsoListParagraph" style="">By reasons of absence of completed Merton's
Energy Assessment Template for Minor Residential Schemes detailing how the
development will meet Merton's minimum requirements, absence of plan drawings
identifying the proposed location of low carbon heat and renewable energy
generation technologies, lack of plans showing any retained, refurbished and
new build element, the applicant has failed to demonstrate that the development
would minimise energy demand, reduce greenhouse gas emissions and maximise
renewable energy generation in accordance with the energy hierarchy. The
proposal therefore fails to demonstrate compliance with National
Decision-Making 2026 Policy CC1, London Plan 2021 Policy SI2 and Merton Local
Plan 2024 Policies CC2.1, CC2.2, CC2.3 and CC2.4.<o:p></o:p></p>
